jobs.title: Analyst or Associate, Wealth Management
jobs.description:
Adams Street Partners (“Adams Street”) is a global private markets investment manager that has nearly $76 billion* in assets under management. The firm is 100% employee-owned, which fosters a positive and unique culture of collaboration, intellectual rigor, integrity, and a commitment to professional development. For the eighth year in a row, Adams Street was named one of Pension & Investments’ Best Places to Work in Money Management in 2025.

Employees operate as a single global team, integrating the expertise of the firm’s investment professionals across five strategies: primary investments, secondary investments, growth equity, private credit, and co-investments.  Adams Street is considered a private markets pioneer and was inducted into the Private Equity Hall of Fame in 2000.

The firm was founded more than 50 years ago, and clients include leading public and corporate pension plans, foundations, endowments, insurance companies, registered investment advisors, and high net worth individuals worldwide.

Adams Street has offices in Abu Dhabi, Austin, Beijing, Boston, Chicago, Hong Kong, London, Munich, Menlo Park, New York, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo and Toronto.

* As of June 30, 2026. Adams Street Partners’ methodology to calculate Assets Under Management (AUM) is based on fund net asset value (NAV), plus unfunded commitments, plus leverage, but excluding the effect of subscription lines of credit. The prior AUM methodology was based on investor commitments minus commitments to fully liquidated underlying partnerships. Such change in methodology was effective July 2026; however, for periods shown prior to December 31, 2025, Adams Street continues to use the previous methodology. This updated methodology more closely aligns with (i) the amount of assets managed on behalf of investors and (ii) the amount of capital available to make direct and/or partnership investments. Amounts stated by investment advisers in regulatory filings (“regulatory AUM”) have a prescribed methodology, which may, in some circumstances, differ from the methodology such adviser uses for other purposes, including marketing efforts. Additional information is available upon request.

Adams Street Partners is actively seeking an Associate to join the Investor Relations Team in Chicago directly supporting the Wealth Sales and Fundraising Teams. Reporting to the Director of Client Service and working alongside other Associates the position will provide a superior level of service to our prospective and existing investors across wealth channels (private banks, wirehouses, broker dealers, RIAs  and family offices), by creating and coordinating effective communications and data. The Associate will engage with teams across Adams Street to support ongoing investor requests and coordinate wealth-related projects. Given Adams Street’s collaborative culture, this role requires exceptional organizational and client servicing skills, with the ability to successfully manage competing priorities.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Develop and maintain strong knowledge of Adams Street product offerings, industry trends, competitive landscape, and the universe of prospective and existing clients across North America

- Create existing and prospective client presentations, market updates, and other types of client related communications

- Prepare and deliver customized client-facing materials in response to prospective and existing client requests

- Ensure the timely delivery of standard and customized data & reporting requests

- Registered product support and servicing including coordination of the set-up and monitoring of the operational infrastructure when launching a product on a platform

- Support the team with marketing efforts including RFPs and due diligence materials and day to day investor inquiries

- Supporting the onboarding and subscription process (including transfers) and engagement with third parties & administrators where appropriate

- Support market and prospect research across the North American region to identify, track and manage pipeline activity

- Serve as one of the point person for the Investor Portal (access to investor portal, data entry) and CRM (Salesforce, including updating client records, tracking opportunities and recording meeting notes)

- Collaborate with teams across the firm to ensure accurate and prompt follow-up to ad hoc projects

Requirements:

We seek an individual who is self-disciplined, detail-oriented, demonstrates creative thinking and has the following characteristics:

- Experience in private markets, preferably in a client-facing role.

- Strong written and verbal communication in English.

- 1-2+ years’ professional experience, ideally within wealth management or other client-facing roles

- Knowledge of HNW/UHNW investors and/or family offices preferred.

- Ability to synthesize complex information and prepare technical materials in a timely manner.

- Exceptional attention to detail, highly organized and able to prioritize and meet deadlines.

- Expert knowledge of MS Office Suite products (i.e. Excel, Powerpoint).

- A professional presence combined with exceptional communication skills to interact effectively with internal teams and external parties.

- Strong work ethic with exceptional attention to detail, highly organized and able to prioritize and meet deadlines.

- Fluency with proprietary databases and software systems, including CRM database systems, ideally Salesforce.

- A highly-motivated self-starter with the ability to work independently and within a team context.

- Graduated from a top-tier undergraduate university, ideally with a business focus.

We offer a competitive U.S. benefits package designed to support health, financial security, and work-life balance. Highlights include medical, dental, and vision coverage; a 401(k) with immediate vesting and employer match; profit sharing; flexible spending accounts (FSA); and paid parental leave, including adoption. Employees also receive generous paid time off, commuter benefits, employer-paid short- and long-term disability and life insurance, and access to additional voluntary benefits.
Illinois Pay Transparency
$85,000 — $110,000 USD

The prior AUM methodology was based on investor commitments minus commitments to fully liquidated underlying partnerships. This updated methodology more closely aligns with (i) the amount of assets managed on behalf of investors and (ii) the amount of capital available to make direct and/or partnership investments. Amounts stated by investment advisers in regulatory filings (“regulatory AUM”) have a prescribed methodology, which may, in some circumstances, differ from the methodology such adviser uses for other purposes, including marketing efforts. Additional information is available upon request.

The Opportunity

This is a rare chance to launch your investment career at the heart of one of the most established primary investment franchises in private markets. As an Analyst on our London Primary Investments Team, you will sit alongside experienced investors evaluating the best private equity and venture capital funds in Europe and beyond – the managers backing the companies shaping the future economy.

From day one, you will be a genuine member of the deal team: forming a view on managers, interrogating track records, and helping decide where our clients’ capital is committed. You will gain exposure across the full breadth of private markets – buyout, growth, and venture, across geographies and sectors – building the judgement and network that define a long-term career as an investor.

What You’ll Do

- Evaluate investment opportunities – assess private equity and venture capital funds, forming a view on manager quality, strategy, and the durability of their edge.

- Dig into the numbers – analyse fund and portfolio performance, track records, value creation, and attribution to understand what truly drives returns.

- Build the investment case – contribute your analysis and conclusions directly to investment memoranda that go in front of our investment committee.

- Develop market intelligence – build a proprietary, forward-looking view of managers, sectors, and themes across European private markets, becoming a genuine expert in your coverage areas.

- Conduct due diligence – play a hands-on role in researching and interrogating new opportunities, working directly with GPs and the broader market.

- Partner across the firm – collaborate with investment colleagues globally and engage with clients and managers, building the relationships that are central to this industry.

Who We’re Looking For

We are looking for a bright, ambitious, and intellectually curious individual excited to build a career as a private markets investor. You will likely have:

- A curious, driven and self-motivated outlook and be able to demonstrate these qualities through a record of achievement, whether academic, professional or self-directed.

- Genuine enthusiasm for private equity and venture capital, and a desire to learn what makes great investors and great companies.

- Sharp analytical ability and strong written communication, with confidence in Excel and PowerPoint.

- Proficiency in the use of AI tools to enhance research, analysis and productivity is also expected.

- A collaborative approach – someone who thinks creatively, and thrives as part of a team.

- A professional presence and strong interpersonal skills to engage effectively with colleagues, clients, and managers.

- This role is London based.

The Primary Investment Team at Adams Street invests in premier buyout and venture capital funds at the time they are being raised. Investing with a broad global mandate and across a range of geographies, stages, and subclasses, the Primary Team has consistently delivered strong risk-adjusted returns and liquidity across multiple business and economic cycles.

The Primary Investment Associate will be responsible for supporting activities involving sourcing, analyzing, and monitoring investment opportunities. The Associate will work closely with our US Primary Investments Team, and the role offers a diversified exposure to private equity and venture capital investing. Specifically, the individual will be involved with and responsible for:

Assist in evaluation and monitoring of investment opportunities:

- Meet with General Partner groups to evaluate potential investment opportunities and monitor existing investments.

- Perform quantitative analysis, including portfolio valuation, comparable company analysis, value driver analysis, performance attribution analysis, and others.

- Good understanding of the private equity and venture capital industry.

- Strong analytical, modeling, organizational, and writing skills.

- A professional presence combined with relationship and communication skills to interact effectively with internal and external parties.

- Self-starter with strong work ethic, who can handle projects from start to finish while negotiating multiple, competing deadlines.

About the Secondary Investment Team

Adams Street’s secondary investment team consists of 19 professionals globally.  To date, Adams Street has closed on over 300 secondary transactions, ranging from traditional acquisitions of limited partnership interests from other private equity fund investors (LP-led transactions) to more complex, structured acquisitions of portfolios of direct company interests and creative liquidity solutions to fund managers (GP-led transactions).

It manages over $8 billion, currently investing its eighth dedicated secondary fund as well as capital from multiple other Adams Street funds of funds and separately managed accounts. The team benefits from the firm’s unique knowledge base and relationships across private markets and its disciplined and balanced approach to investing have generated exceptional long-term returns that have outperformed private equity industry benchmarks on a consistent basis.

Responsibilities:

The Secondary Investment Associate is responsible for analyzing, modeling, and monitoring investment opportunities. The position offers a deal-oriented, high-responsibility role exposed to the full array of private markets subclasses, including buyout, venture capital, and credit funds across all industries and in both developed and emerging markets. Secondary Associates are deeply involved in the development of valuation and cash flow models, investment theses, and various risk analyses. This role will be based in either our Chicago or New York office.

Specifically, the individual will be involved with and responsible for:

- Performing quantitative analysis, including LBO, fund, and transaction modeling

- Conducting market and company research

- Participating in due diligence calls with GPs, management, and sellers

- Assisting in all aspects of the transaction, including deal selection, pricing analysis, and execution

- Assisting in all transaction documentation and presentations to investment committee

- Developing and maintaining proprietary deal and market intelligence

- Performing deal monitoring analysis

- Supporting in strategic team and firm initiatives

Venture Growth Team Overview

Adams Street’s Venture Growth team backs ambitious founders building the technology and healthcare companies shaping the future. We invest in startups that have achieved meaningful scale while maintaining rapid growth in enormous markets.

Over five decades, the advantages of our firm’s integrated private markets platform – across direct and fund investing – have continued to compound. Leveraging deep market intelligence and longstanding relationships with the world’s leading venture firms, our Venture Growth team has been able to invest behind breakout companies across successive innovation cycles, including today’s AI inflection point. We’re proudly invested in companies such as: Baseten, ClickHouse, Glean, Zip, Fractile, Kalshi, Parloa, Altruist, Quince, Nourish, Equip Health, BillionToOne (Nasdaq: BLLN), Turquoise Health, among many others. Our team consists of 12 individuals working out of our Menlo Park office.

Venture Growth – Investment Associate, Technology:

The Venture Growth team is actively recruiting for a technology Investment Associate position in our Menlo Park, CA office. The Associate will serve as a core member of our lean deal teams (often just Partner + Associate) and contribute across the full investment lifecycle – from thesis development and sourcing through diligence, execution, and portfolio monitoring.

The individual will primarily be involved with and responsible for:

- All aspects of investment due diligence: business, market, management, competitive, financial/returns modeling, cap table analysis and legal diligence

- Conducting extensive market research to bring sector insights to the team and identify potential new investment opportunities in the technology ecosystem

- Developing relationships with leading private companies by attending conferences and proactively meeting with entrepreneurs and other investors

- Preparing investment memoranda and presenting analysis and recommendations to the Investment Committee

- Working on selected internal processes and strategic initiatives

Requirements:

- 2-4 years of experience in technology investment banking, consulting, principal investing (mid/late-stage VC, growth equity or PE), or analytical experience at a high-growth technology company

- Demonstrated enthusiasm for technology and emerging business models; active tracking of important companies, products, and market developments to form independent views about where technology is headed

- High-ownership, detail-oriented self-starter who can manage multiple workstreams and competing deadlines

- Advanced analytical / quantitative ability and excel modeling skills

- Outstanding relationship-building and communication skills to engage effectively with founders, investors, and other internal and external stakeholders

- Ability to structure and present complex ideas and information in a simple persuasive form, both written and orally

About the Team

The Portfolio Finance team focuses on deal funding, liquidity, and financing across Adams Street’s Private Equity and Private Credit investment strategies. The team manages day to day cash optimization, credit facilities, NAV facilities, and long-term forecasting with a focus on risk management and the performance of our funds.

The role of Vice President will be a leadership role within the team, with firm-wide responsibility across both our Private Equity and Private Credit strategies. The Vice President will be expected to collaborate with various teams across the firm, drive policy, control, and efficiency within the team.

Responsibilities:

- Work with Private Equity and Private Credit investment teams, Investment Strategy & Risk Management (ISRM), Operations, Accounting, and Tax teams to optimize liquidity and usage of financing for Adams Street’s portfolios (evergreen, closed ended and custom mandates)

- Build and maintain forward looking models to project cash flows from new deal pipeline, capital inflows/outflows, asset lifecycle events and financing transactions to help plan deployment strategy

- Monitor portfolios and take actions to manage cash levels, financing facilities, target leverage and key performance metrics

- Work with Adams Street lenders to source and negotiate subscription line, NAV, and asset backed credit facilities

- Work across various internal teams to coordinate the sourcing, maintenance, and accuracy of projections used in making economic decisions

- Build and monitor portfolio risk metrics to measure against pre-established risk guidelines (e.g. leverage, cash levels) in growing and dynamic portfolios

- Manage FX Hedging processes across our investment portfolio

- Direct and mentor Associates and Senior Associates supporting the team

Candidate Requirements:

We seek an individual who is self-disciplined, demonstrates creative thinking and has the following characteristics:

- At least 5 years (Senior Associate) / 7 years (Vice President) of investment management experience and minimum 3 years managing private market processes and portfolios (including permanent/open ended capital structures)

- Experience with private markets credit facilities preferred

- Advanced degrees with a background in quantitative finance/modeling preferred

- Structured finance experience is a plus

- Strong quantitative, analytical, critical thinking and problem-solving skills with a financial engineering mindset

- Familiarity with treasury and financing function, products and providers

- Experience communicating and collaborating across multiple internal and external stakeholders

- Maintains accuracy and quality when working within tight deadlines

- Experienced user of programming languages (e.g. R), database design, and developer of analytical tools are desirable

- Ability to prioritize and independently execute assigned projects while directing and managing support staff

This is a senior leadership role for a proven writer and people manager who can both produce the firm's most complex, highest-stakes executive RFP responses and set the strategy, standards, and team structure that allow Adams Street to compete at scale as one of the world's premier private markets investment managers.

The ideal candidate combines exceptional writing craft with strong business judgment, executive presence, and demonstrated success managing and developing a team. While executive RFPs, RFIs, and DDQs remain the core of the function, this leader will also own a broader portfolio of firmwide business communications, partnering closely with Marketing, Investor Relations, Compliance, Investment teams, and senior firm leadership, including Partners.

This is a hybrid role based in Chicago, with a flexible mix of remote and in-office work.

What You Will Do

Team & Function Leadership

- Own the strategy, quality, and day-to-day execution of Adams Street's global RFP, RFI, and DDQ program across all product lines and regions

- Manage, mentor, and develop a team of RFP and Business Communications professionals, providing hands-on coaching on writing, business judgment, and career growth

- Set priorities and allocate resources across the team's active pipeline, balancing workload, deadlines, and business priority across a high-volume, deadline-driven request queue

- Serve as the primary point of escalation and final quality control for the most complex, highest-visibility, and largest-mandate opportunities

- Represent the function in cross-functional governance forums and drive alignment on process, roles, and standards across Investor Relations, Investment teams, and Shared Services

Executive-Level Writing & Content Ownership

- Produce and edit executive-level responses for the firm's most sensitive and complex RFPs, RFIs, DDQs, and firm awards

- Clearly articulate Adams Street's investment capabilities, processes, performance, and thought leadership to institutional and wealth audiences

- Partner directly with subject matter experts, senior Investment professionals, and Partners to translate complex investment concepts into clear, persuasive, client-ready messaging

- Own governance and quality standards for the RFP and content management system, ensuring resources remain accurate, current, and consistent firmwide

Process, Technology & Reporting

- Drive continuous improvement of RFP processes, tools, and content infrastructure (including content management and AI-assisted drafting platforms), identifying and implementing efficiency gains

- Develop and present reporting on RFP volume, win rates, and pipeline health to senior stakeholders and firm leadership

- Maintain deep, current expertise in Adams Street's private markets strategies and platform

- Ensure all written deliverables across the team are accurate, timely, and aligned with the firm's brand and quality standards

Collaboration & Stakeholder Management

- Collaborate seamlessly with colleagues across the US, Europe, and Asia

- Build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders across Investor Relations, Compliance, and the Investment teams

- Respond to, and manage team responses to, requests and escalations from prospects, consultants, clients, GPs, and internal stakeholders

Essential Qualities

- Bachelor's degree in business, marketing, communications, or a finance-related field required

- Minimum of 8 years of progressive experience in RFP/proposal management, marketing communications, or investor relations, with proven success in investment management, private markets, consulting, investment banking, or financial services

- Demonstrated people-management experience, with a track record of building, mentoring, and developing high-performing writers and analysts

- Exceptional writing and editing skills — clear, concise, persuasive, and adaptable across executive, client, and consultant audiences

- Strong executive presence and the judgment and credibility to influence senior stakeholders, including Partners and senior Investment professionals

- Proven project management skills, with the ability to prioritize a high-volume pipeline and lead a team through sustained deadline pressure

- Strategic mindset, with experience driving process improvement and adoption of RFP/content management technology (e.g., Salesforce, Loopio, or similar platforms)

- Strong working knowledge of private markets strategies (primaries, secondaries, co-investments, private credit, growth equity) strongly preferred

- Positive energy, intellectual curiosity, and a collaborative, team-oriented leadership style

- Experience partnering with Compliance/Legal on regulatory and disclosure considerations in client communications is a plus

We offer a competitive U.S. benefits package designed to support health, financial security, and work-life balance. Highlights include medical, dental, and vision coverage; a 401(k) with immediate vesting and employer match; profit sharing; flexible spending accounts (FSA); and paid parental leave, including adoption. Employees also receive generous paid time off, commuter benefits, employer-paid short- and long-term disability and life insurance, and access to additional voluntary benefits.

jobs.title: Vice President, Primary
jobs.description:
Adams Street Partners (“Adams Street”) is a global private markets investment manager that has nearly $76 billion* in assets under management. The firm is 100% employee-owned, which fosters a positive and unique culture of collaboration, intellectual rigor, integrity, and a commitment to professional development. For the eighth year in a row, Adams Street was named one of Pension & Investments’ Best Places to Work in Money Management in 2025.

Employees operate as a single global team, integrating the expertise of the firm’s investment professionals across five strategies: primary investments, secondary investments, growth equity, private credit, and co-investments.  Adams Street is considered a private markets pioneer and was inducted into the Private Equity Hall of Fame in 2000.

The firm was founded more than 50 years ago, and clients include leading public and corporate pension plans, foundations, endowments, insurance companies, registered investment advisors, and high net worth individuals worldwide.

Adams Street has offices in Abu Dhabi, Austin, Beijing, Boston, Chicago, Hong Kong, London, Munich, Menlo Park, New York, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo and Toronto.

* As of June 30, 2026. Adams Street Partners’ methodology to calculate Assets Under Management (AUM) is based on fund net asset value (NAV), plus unfunded commitments, plus leverage, but excluding the effect of subscription lines of credit. The prior AUM methodology was based on investor commitments minus commitments to fully liquidated underlying partnerships. Such change in methodology was effective July 2026; however, for periods shown prior to December 31, 2025, Adams Street continues to use the previous methodology. This updated methodology more closely aligns with (i) the amount of assets managed on behalf of investors and (ii) the amount of capital available to make direct and/or partnership investments. Amounts stated by investment advisers in regulatory filings (“regulatory AUM”) have a prescribed methodology, which may, in some circumstances, differ from the methodology such adviser uses for other purposes, including marketing efforts. Additional information is available upon request.

Overview:

This position offers an excellent opportunity for an Investment Professional with proven financial, analytical and interpersonal skills and an interest in the alternative investment sector, to be part of a premier global investment firm that provides investment services to institutional clients.  The individual selected for this position will be based in the firm’s Menlo Park, CA offices. They will be a part of a team managing a large portfolio of venture capital funds  (limited partnerships) and will be responsible for supporting the team’s identification and management of a global portfolio of venture managers.

Specifically, the individual will be involved with and responsible for:

Sourcing & Evaluation

- Meet with general partner groups to evaluate potential investment opportunities.

- Manage deal flow across global venture capital portfolio with a focus on venture capital funds.

- Conduct market research on investment sectors and themes.

Execution & Due Diligence

- Lead and conduct due diligence; identify key investment merits and considerations through qualitative and quantitative analysis, meetings with fund managers, strategy review, reference checks and on-site visits, etc.

- Perform due diligence on growth-stage co- investments.

- Prepare memoranda and participate in investment discussions with internal investment committee.

- Work with counsel to negotiate partnership terms and coordinate the closing process.

- Support construction and evaluation of fund portfolios.

Leadership

- Thought leadership on investment and industry trends.

- Help author internal and external research and thought pieces.

- Mentor and manage junior team members.

Monitoring

- Attend annual meetings.

- Review quarterly reports and related materials.

- Document compliance with investment guidelines.

- Monitor investment forward pipeline and allocation planning.

Business Support & Investor Relations

- Support the firm’s marketing efforts through new business presentations to potential clients and consultants.

- Market the firm’s capabilities to market participants to generate secondary and direct growth-stage deal flow.

- Support investor relationships for existing global venture mandates.

- Support firm initiatives as they relate to the firm’s business plans.

- Contribute positively to Adams Street’s culture and thought leadership.

Required Skills

The ideal candidate will be a well-rounded business professional with proven work experience investing and a record of success at a top institution focused on technology investments in primary (partnership) private investments and/or in secondaries and/or in direct investments. The candidate will be a highly motivated professional who sets and meets ambitious business and personal commitments with a demonstrated interest in building a career in venture capital investing.

In addition, the candidate will have:

- 6-8 years of investing analysis and due diligence experience. Prior fund experience is preferred, though not required, and broader investment experience will be considered.

- Experience investing in technology sector (via fund investments, co- investments , or secondaries).

- MBA or similar advanced degree is preferred but not required.

- A facility to elicit in an informed, challenging, and effective manner the critical variables that will determine an investment’s financial success or failure.

- Strong modeling, organizational and writing skills.

- Deep understanding of trends and issues in the private equity industry and venture sector, specifically technology, both U.S. and global.

- The ability to synthesize complex data in a clear manner.

- A professional presence coupled with relationship skills to interact effectively with clients, general partners and colleagues at all levels.

- The ability to work independently while operating within a highly integrated global team context.

- A willingness to establish a position and confidence of convictions as it relates to investment decisions.

- Desire to build a career in venture capital investing required.

- Intellectual curiosity, demonstrated contribution to thought leadership, and forward thinking.

- Willingness to travel domestically and internationally.

- Maturity, a self-starter with a desire and ability to work in a global, fast-paced, collaborative, high-performing team environment while managing a wide range of responsibilities.

We offer a competitive U.S. benefits package designed to support health, financial security, and work-life balance. Highlights include medical, dental, and vision coverage; a 401(k) with immediate vesting and employer match; profit sharing; flexible spending accounts (FSA); and paid parental leave, including adoption. Employees also receive generous paid time off, commuter benefits, employer-paid short- and long-term disability and life insurance, and access to additional voluntary benefits.

$150,000 — $200,000 USD
